description:
Redwood Inference will build an internal “unit economics” dashboard that standardizes how the company measures blended cost of inference as $/1M output tokens and enables drilldowns by model, region, and customer tier. The dashboard is intended to be the source of truth for product decisions (pricing/packaging, routing defaults, rollout guardrails), finance reporting (gross margin and capacity efficiency), and engineering optimization work (batching, caching, and quantization profiles).

Goals:
- Provide a consistent, finance-aligned definition of blended $/1M output tokens (including compute, cache hit effects, overhead allocation, and discounts/credits policy as appropriate).
- Enable drilldowns and slice-and-dice views by: model family/variant, region, customer tier (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise), and optionally route/config (batching/caching/quantization profile) to connect optimization levers to unit cost.
- Make data trustworthy: clear lineage, reconciliation to billing/metering, and guardrails for metric cardinality and late-arriving data.
- Support decision workflows: weekly review cadence, alerting for regressions, and an “explain” panel that attributes deltas to drivers (region mix shift, model mix shift, cache hit-rate changes, quant profile adoption).

Scope (phase-based):
1) Metric definition + data contracts (2–3 weeks): align on formulas, required dimensions, data freshness/SLA, and reconciliation methodology with billing hooks.
2) Data pipeline + semantic layer (3–4 weeks): build/extend telemetry aggregation for cost attribution at token level; publish curated datasets for Console/BI; implement tier/model/region mapping tables.
3) Dashboard UI + drilldowns (3–4 weeks): implement charts, filters, cohort comparisons, and exportable views for Finance and Product.
4) Launch + ops (1–2 weeks): documentation, runbooks, alerts for data health, and a weekly unit economics review.

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Aditya Rao (Optimize)
- Engineering: Logan Wright (Telemetry & Analytics Platform), Nadia Rahman (Telemetry), Caleb Johnson (Observability Data)
- Finance: Laura Bennett (CFO), Rishi Malhotra (FP&A)
- SRE/Observability: Allison Grant, Aisha Bello
- Applied ML: Jonas Weber / Karthik Iyer / Arjun Desai (to link quantization profiles to unit economics)

Constraints & risks:
- Attribution correctness: mapping GPU/fleet costs to requests must be explicit and auditable; backfills and late data must be handled.
- Dimensionality/cardinality: model+region+customer+route dimensions can explode; must define supported drilldowns and aggregation rules.
- Consistency with billing: dashboard must reconcile with metering and invoice-level totals within an agreed tolerance.
- Access control: some views (customer-tier and pricing/discount impacts) should be restricted to finance/product leadership.

files.description: PRD: problem statement, users (Finance/Product/Eng), key workflows, success metrics, MVP vs V2 scope, and launch criteria for the $/1M output tokens dashboard.
Console UX spec: information architecture, filter model (model/region/tier), drilldown navigation, and annotated mock descriptions for key charts and tables.
Data contracts: required dimensions, metric definitions, freshness SLOs, known limitations (late events, sampling), and ownership for each upstream dataset.
ADR documenting the canonical definition of blended $/1M output tokens, allocation approach (compute + overhead), exclusions, and reconciliation strategy with billing.
SLO doc for the dashboard datasets (freshness, completeness, reconciliation error bounds), plus alert thresholds and escalation paths.
Finance-facing KPI guide: how FP&A should interpret blended cost, tie-outs to COGS, and how mix-shifts (model/region/tier) affect reported metrics.
Guide linking quantization profiles to unit economics: required tags/metadata, how to attribute savings, and caveats around quality vs cost trade-offs.
Runbook: backfilling unit economics datasets, verifying reconciliation, and safely reprocessing historical partitions without breaking dashboards.
Working doc: early brainstorming on which charts matter (blended cost trend, cost by driver, cache hit impact), open questions, and rough sketches.
Draft data dictionary: field definitions, joins, grain, and examples of queries for model/region/tier drilldowns.
Engineering notes: pipeline options (stream vs batch), partition strategy, late-event handling, and cardinality constraints.
Sheet-style doc: reconciliation table comparing dashboard totals vs billing/metering totals by day/region/tier, with variance notes.
Template for the weekly unit economics review: KPIs, mix-shift sections, notable regressions, and action items.
MVP scope doc for Product: prioritized drilldowns, must-have export formats, and what’s explicitly deferred.
Notes connecting batching/caching/quantization levers to expected unit cost movement; hypotheses to validate post-launch.
Tracker (sheet-like): quantization profile rollout/adoption by model family and region, intended to be joined into unit economics drilldowns.
Slides draft for internal demo: narrative explaining metric definitions, how to use drilldowns, and examples of insights.
Epic/parent ticket: “Internal unit economics dashboard” with objectives, milestones, and cross-team dependencies.
Define canonical metrics and acceptance criteria with Finance (tie-out requirements, variance tolerance, inclusion/exclusion rules).
Access control policy for dashboard views (restricted slices for pricing/discount impacts); coordinate with Finance leadership.
Design ticket: dashboard layout, filter UX, drilldown navigation, and empty/loading/error states for data freshness issues.
Design ticket: “Explain cost delta” panel UI (driver attribution, mix shift breakdown, links to related rollouts/incidents).
Implement dataset: daily blended $/1M output tokens by model/region/tier with agreed grain and partitioning.
Add tier mapping table (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise) with historical correctness and backfill plan.
Integrate quantization profile tags into telemetry aggregation so unit cost can be sliced by quant profile.
Add cache metrics (prefix/KV hit rate, cache savings estimate) into unit economics semantic layer.
Build reconciliation job comparing aggregated unit-econ totals vs billing/metering totals; alert on variance > threshold.
Dashboard backend API: query endpoints for drilldowns (model/region/tier) with pagination and caching.
Console UI implementation: charts, tables, filters, and shareable links for specific slices.
Add data quality monitoring (freshness/completeness checks) and wire alerts to #eng-sre and #eng-platform.
Backfill historical data (90 days) and validate against Finance’s expected totals; document known gaps.
Performance task: control cardinality and query latency for drilldowns (pre-aggregations, caching, query limits).
Rollout plan: internal feature flag, staged enablement for Finance/Product, and post-launch feedback loop.
Security review: ensure restricted metrics (discount impacts, account-level slices) are gated; audit access logs.
PR: Add unit economics aggregation job (daily partitions) producing blended $/1M output tokens with model/region/tier dimensions; includes schema and tests.
PR: Introduce semantic layer views for unit economics (stable column names, documented joins) and deprecate older ad-hoc queries.
PR: Add quantization_profile and runtime_config tags to metering events; propagate through ingestion to analytics tables.
PR: Implement reconciliation job vs billing hooks with alerting on variance thresholds; includes runbook links and backfill tooling.
PR: Console UI for unit economics dashboard (filters, charts, drilldowns) behind internal feature flag; includes screenshot stubs.
PR: Add cache hit-rate metrics and estimated savings attribution to unit economics dataset; update documentation in-code.
PR: New dashboards/alerts for unit-econ pipeline freshness/completeness and reconciliation variance; wiring to oncall notifications.
PR: Query performance improvements (pre-aggregations, result caching, guardrails on high-cardinality filters).
PR: Add role-based access controls for restricted unit economics slices and log/audit access for compliance.
